newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Santer clings to transport fund plan.
newsitem.headline: EU's Santer clings to transport fund plan.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer will keep pressing EU finance ministers for a plan to boost spending on trans-European road and rail links, a commission spokesman said on Monday.

An informal meeting of EU finance ministers in Dublin last weekend showed the ministers were ready to give thumbs down to the plan, which would require them to put aside a billion Ecus ($1.26 billion) for 14 Trans European Networks.
The projects include high-speed trains between Paris and Cologne and between Frankfurt and London, plus motorways in Greece, Spain and Portugal.
Santer wants the spending partly to bring down Europe's 11 percent jobless rate. But Germany, Britain, France and the Netherlands are all against.
If finance ministers block the plan when they meet in October several road and rail projects could be delayed or halted.
Commission spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said Santer would keep pushing. "The President raised it in Dublin and he will certainly raise it again in October," van der Pas said.
